title: signal-sampler-quickdigest-and-probe-bundle-2026-06-16
body:
Purpose

Quick digest of recent field signals (May–Jun 2026) and compact probe bundle suggestions. This doc is intentionally terse — aim is to hand an eng owner a prioritized list of small-to-medium experiments that reduce customer friction and reveal unit-cost tradeoffs.

Methodology and sources
- Inputs: 27 customer conversations (CS notes), 12 support tickets flagged as 'inference-quirk', latency traces from Console (sampled per-customer), and logs from KV-cache opt-in experiments.
- Lens: severity-to-frequency (how many accounts affected) + cost-to-implementation (S/M/L) + regression risk (low/med/high).
- Output: 6 candidate probes (microfeatures + config tweaks) with suggested owners and acceptance criteria.

Topline summary (1-liner)
Customers cluster around three friction themes: 1) unexpected token-cost spikes for short prompts, 2) KV-cache warmup inconsistencies across model variants, 3) rollout safety/config discoverability for fallbacks. Each has quick probes that can be shipped within 2–6 weeks.

Representative customer quotes
- "We saw costs jump overnight when a routing fallback switched to a longer-ctx model — no one told us." (mid-market fintech)
- "Sometimes the chat continues to echo earlier system instructions — cache seems stale or misrouted." (AI-native startup)
- "I need a toggle to prefer latency over cost for specific routes, not bucket-wide." (platform team)

Signal matrix (condensed)
- Short-prompt token spikes: frequency = 8 customers, severity = medium, suggested probe: short-prefix-billing-sampler (S).
- KV-cache warmup variance: frequency = 11 customers, severity = high for stateful chat, suggested probe: aggressive-kv-prefetch toggle (M).
- Fallback surprise (longer model): frequency = 6 customers, severity = high (cost), suggested probe: explicit-fallback-notification + per-route caps (M).
- Route-level SLO mismatch: frequency = 5, severity = low, suggested probe: route-preference-UI nodal tweak (S).
- Embedding-dimensional drift (subset of dedicated customers): frequency = 3, severity = medium, suggested probe: embedding-compatibility-check on model-upgrade (M).

Prioritized probe bundle (ranked)
1) short-prefix-billing-sampler (impact: medium, cost: S, owner: CS + Eng-console)
   - What it does: instrument short prompts (<64 tokens) to log unexpected per-token multipliers and surface anomalies in Console billing views.
   - Acceptance criteria: 90% of sampled anomalies link back to a route/model change; two customer alerts surfaced in 2 weeks; dashboard shows delta vs baseline.
   - Why fast: telemetry-only; uses existing billing pipes.

2) aggressive-kv-prefetch toggle (impact: high for chat UX, cost: M, owner: Eng-serving-runtime)
   - What it does: server-side opt-in flag that warms KV cache for pinned conversation prefixes and pins recent KV pages after every response (configurable TTL).
   - Acceptance criteria: median first-token latency for stateful chats drops by 30% in pilot customers; no memory leaks after 72h; no +10% token cost for standard use.

3) explicit-fallback-notification + per-route caps (impact: high cost control, cost: M, owner: Product-hosted-api & Eng-routing)
   - What it does: when smart-routing chooses a model variant with higher per-token cost, surface a non-blocking notification to customers and allow per-route override caps.
   - Acceptance criteria: reduce 'billing surprise' tickets by 75% for pilot cohort; per-route cap respected in 100% of routed requests in tests.

4) route-preference-UI nodal tweak (impact: low, cost: S, owner: Eng-console)
   - What it does: expose a concise toggle (latency/cost/throughput) on route config pages with clear tooltips and link to docs.
   - Acceptance criteria: 50% reduction in docs-linked support threads about route intent in 1 month.

5) embedding-compatibility-check on model-upgrade (impact: med, cost: M, owner: Eng-optimize)
   - What it does: when a customer pins an embedding model upgrade, run a shadow-compatibility test (similarity delta on a small labeled sample) and surface a pass/fail + delta score.
   - Acceptance criteria: reduce mismatched-embedding tickets by 80% for pilot customers; automated pass/fail threshold documented.

Engineering notes and rough effort estimation
- short-prefix-billing-sampler: purely telemetry; 3–5 dev-days, minimal infra.
- aggressive-kv-prefetch: runtime change + feature flag + unit tests; 2 engineers x 3 sprints for safe rollout (pilot behind flag).
- explicit-fallback-notification: routing + console UI + docs + billing hooks; cross-team (routing, console, billing) coordination — estimated 4–6 sprints including QA.
- route-preference-UI: UI + small backend toggle; 1 engineer + 1 UX for 2 sprints.
- embedding-compatibility-check: pipelined evaluation job + UI result; 2 engineers x 3 sprints.

Potential risks and mitigations
- KV-prefetch memory pressure: mitigate with TTL and soft caps; circuit-breaker to revert to current behaviour when memory crosses threshold.
- Notification spam causing churn: make fallback-notifications opt-in per-account initially; provide clear mitigation path and link to a simulation page.
- False positives in embedding compatibility: require manual review for first 5 upgrades per customer and tune thresholds.

Quick experimental design (for aggressive-kv-prefetch pilot)
- Pilot cohort: 6 paying customers with stateful chat traffic; 2-week A/B experiment behind the feature flag.
- Metrics: first-token latency (p95, p50), average tokens per session, memory usage per host, customer-reported regressions.
- Success threshold: p50 latency down by >=20% without >5% increase in per-session token count.

Next steps (who does what)
- CS: circulate this digest to pilot candidates and collect explicit opt-ins (Miguel, Aisha). Deadline: 2026-06-22.
- Eng-console: scope telemetry dashboard for short-prefix-billing-sampler (Lena). ETA: 2 weeks.
- Eng-serving-runtime: schedule design sync for kv-prefetch (owner: TBD in runtime team).
- Product: draft rollout policy for explicit-fallback-notifications and per-route caps (owner: Priya N.).

Open questions for exec/context
- Do we want fallback-notifications enabled by default for new customers or opt-in? (provisional recommendation: opt-in for existing; default-on for new signups with clear consent).
- Should route-level preference toggles be part of the API as a flag (for infra customers) or console-only first? (Recommendation: API-first, UI to follow).

Appendix: quick log snippets and customer traces (sanitized)
- Trace A (mid-market fintech): step: routing decision -> selected: model-x-16k -> token-multiplier spike +38% compared to previous day. No explicit config change in account audit log.
- Trace B (startup): repeated echo of system instruction after reconnection; cold KV page not populated.

Notes to self (CS)
- Keep this doc compact and iterate — convert to Confluence if Pilot succeeds.
- Follow-up cadence: weekly sync with Eng-serving-runtime until kv-prefetch pilot completes.
summary: Compact synthesis of customer signals (May–Jun 2026) with six prioritized probe suggestions designed to reduce billing surprises, improve chat latency via KV-cache warmup, and increase route control discoverability. Includes acceptance criteria, owners, risk notes, and next steps.
